chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Birth in the French Quarter
summary: Danny was born in the French Quarter in 1909, delivered by his midwife grandmother Victoria Barker.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: Uh-huh. You just go ahead on... First let's start with where were you born, Danny?

I was born here in New Orleans, in the French Quarter. That's on... If you have ever been to New Orleans, you will see I was smack dab... I'm a smack-dab original native of the city. I was born right in the section where the city was founded. It's called the French Quarter, the first square mile of New Orleans.

My grandmother and grandfather resided there, and my grandmother was my wife's midwife. She was a midwife for Vernon(?) Hand, and midwife for most of the women who would get calls of emergency. Most of the time they would call old Miss Barker, because she knew how to handle situations of childbirth and distress and panicking. And she was my mother's midwife. My mother was going to...prepared to go to the hospital to have me and make the (?). She said, "Don't worry about it; I'll be your midwife." So just about when the confinement came up, Mother went and resided with her. And my grandmother brought me in this world, Mrs. Barker -- Victoria Barker.
Victoria Barker. And what year was that? What's that date?
Night people. Born at night. 9:30 my mother.
